abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized oncology; however, emerging therapeutic resistance and the pharmacokinetic limitations of monoclonal antibodies necessitate the development of potent, small-molecule alternatives. CMTM6 (CKLF-like MARVEL transmembrane domain-containing protein 6) has recently been identified as a master posttranslational regulator of PD-L1 stability. Here, we characterize GIC-001 and its derivative, GIC-005, as first-in-class small-molecule inhibitors that directly target CMTM6. GIC-001 binds directly to CMTM6, competitively disrupting its association with PD-L1 and the glutamine transporter SLC1A5 (ASCT2) while crucially preserving its interaction with the essential costimulatory ligand CD58. This targeted dissociation facilitates the polyubiquitination and subsequent lysosomal degradation of both PD-L1 and SLC1A5. Consequently, pharmacological inhibition of the CMTM6 axis blunts PD-L1 expression, restricts glutamine uptake in tumor cells, and restores T cell-mediated cytotoxicity. In syngeneic MC38 and Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) models, GIC-001 significantly suppressed tumor progression and prolonged overall survival. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed that this efficacy is driven by a profound remodeling of the tumor microenvironment (TME), characterized by the notable expansion of effector and memory CD8+ T cells alongside the repolarization of suppressive macrophages toward an activated phenotype. Furthermore, GIC-001 exhibited durable antitumor efficacy as a monotherapy and synergized with anti-PD-L1 antibodies, and GIC-005 demonstrated potent in vivo activity. Our findings establish CMTM6-targeted small molecules as a distinct class of dual-action agents that integrate immune and metabolic checkpoint modulation, providing a transformative strategy for cancer immunotherapy.
